excerpt: A cerebellum-like organization with three modules of eight elements yields three separate complexes with low values of Φ (Φ = 20 bits), and a large complex encompassing all the elements has an extremely low Φ value of 5 bits. A reticular element providing common input to a thalamocortical-like main complex has a combined 9-element complex with much lower Φ (Φ = 10 bits), while the thalamocortical-like main complex remains high (Φ = 61 bits). Afferent and efferent pathways can affect the main complex while the larger combined complex has low Φ (Φ = 10 bits).
overview: Figure 4 grounds two linked claims: modular architectures can be information-rich yet poor in integration, and external input/output systems can influence a conscious complex without becoming part of it. The evidence explains why the cerebellum, brainstem arousal systems, sensory pathways, and motor pathways are assigned different constitutive roles despite their causal importance.
title: Modular And Port Architectures
